entries.not_relevant_because: The margulis-conjecture entry asks for classification of ergodic A-invariant probability measures for higher-rank diagonalizable actions on homogeneous spaces G/Γ, with the conclusion that each such measure is algebraic. Both manuscripts concern a different conjecture that carries Margulis's name: the Margulis–Platonov conjecture, which says that noncentral abstract normal subgroups of G(k) are pullbacks of open normal subgroups of the finite product of anisotropic local groups. Neither manuscript mentions ergodic theory, invariant measures on G/Γ, Cartan or diagonal actions, or the Furstenberg, Katok–Spatzier, Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss or Einsiedler conjectures; a keyword search of both build folders found only arithmetic uses of 'homogeneous space' (torsors and the Hasse principle). The only probability-measure material is an auxiliary translation-invariant law on finite colourings of unitary elements, built to prove the normal-subgroup result, not a classification of A-invariant measures. The matching pass's 'other' flag was right: this family is the Margulis–Platonov normal subgroup conjecture, not the measure-classification conjecture.
